sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Pet Supplies and Pet Care Devices

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier, Articles L561-1 to L561-6 and L561-45 to L561-56; Décret n°2017-1094 du 8 juin 2017 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Ordonnance n°2016-1635 du 1er décembre 2016; Code de commerce, Article L123-11-2; French AML/CFT supervision by ACPR.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or bank of country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-bankruptcy and no criminal record for directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal record office (casier judiciaire) or competent justice authority of country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, French national sanctions and FICOBA files, UN Security Council resolutions, OFAC SDN List (for USD-denominated payment rails), and ACPR regulatory warnings. Screening must be repeated at least every 30 days and upon any change of ownership or control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be written in Latin script. It may use French or any language, but if not in French, a French translation must be filed. The name must not be contrary to French public policy or create confusion with existing trademarks or registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days. A final refusal may be challenged before the competent Tribunal judiciaire. Alternatively, a revised name can be filed immediately through Guichet Unique without additional filing fees.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for e-commerce under Article L123-11-2 of the Commercial Code. The company must execute a valid domiciliation agreement with an approved domicile service provider and maintain a physical address for receipt of official mail. A virtual office is acceptable provided that the place of effective management does not compromise French tax residence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (≈5% chance) for this low-risk non-licensed e-commerce activity; unannounced physical inspections by DGFiP or URSSAF are uncommon but legally possible.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SAS articles of association and legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (fixed and hourly fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and INPI trademark clearance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign documents (4 documents)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de Commerce (French Commercial Code) — general incorporation arts. L.210-1 to L.210-3; SAS-specific regime arts. L.227-1 to L.227-20; registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés per arts. L.123-1, L.123-7 and R.123-8 to R.123-30; unified filing procedures under Order No. 2022-1513 (Guichet Unique).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (single business-formalities window) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); downstream registration executed by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Single Incorporation Dossier (Dossier Unique de Création d'Entreprise) comprising the Statuts (Articles of Association), the share-capital deposit certificate, the legal-announcement certificate, and the beneficial-owner declaration, filed online at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital for SAS (art. L.227-1); capital is freely fixed in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation and deposited in a blocked account with a French credit institution or with the Caisse des Dépôts, evidenced by a bank certificate of funds release included in the filing dossier. Non-cash contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation report (commissaire aux apports) if the value exceeds EUR 30,000 or represents more than half of the capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital be fixed at [EUR] [amount], divided into [N] shares of EUR [nominal] each, in cash, subscribed and fully paid up by the founding shareholders, as evidenced by the attached blocked-funds bank certificate; RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [address], France; RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President for an indefinite term, with full powers to bind the Company; [Name] be appointed General Manager; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the President be authorized to complete all incorporation formalities, including the Guichet Unique filing, legal announcement publication, and the Kbis, SIREN/SIRET, and French VAT registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the French Statuts (Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate lawyer / law firm; notarisation only mandatory if real-estate contributions are made; otherwise a privately signed deed suffices.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French containing company name, corporate object (electronic retailing of pet supplies and pet-care devices), registered-office address, share capital breakdown, transferability of shares, corporate-governance provisions (President's powers, shareholders' collective decisions, voting rights). Circulate the final text to the founding shareholders, obtain wet-ink or e-signature of all shareholders, and execute the appointment letters of the President and General Manager.
required_dossiers: Statuts executed by all founding shareholders
Shareholders' identification documents (passports) and proof of residence
Letter of acceptance of office signed by the President
Letter of acceptance of office signed by the General Manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe or INPI raises a legal irregularity in the Statuts, amend by way of a corrective deed rectifying the defective clauses, re-execute, and resubmit to the dossier within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a French Bank Account and Deposit of the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French licensed credit institution (e.g., traditional bank or online business bank) or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) where account-opening is refused.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation file to the chosen bank; instruct the bank to open a professional blocked account in the name of the company under incorporation and deposit the full subscribed cash capital. Obtain the certificate of funds deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds / certificat de blocage) naming the bank, the depositor, and the amount, which is required for the incorporation filing. After Kbis issuance, request release of funds to the company's free current account.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts
Passports / valid identity documents of all shareholders and signatories
Proof of address of the future registered office
Beneficial-owner declaration (identification of natural persons holding ultimately >25% of the company)
Business plan or bank's KYC questionnaire if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a commercial bank refuses account opening (common for newly incorporated entities), apply to the Comité Consultatif du Secteur Financier or use the CDC consignation procedure to deposit the capital; the CDC issues a certificat de consignation equivalent to a bank certificate for RCS purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Mandatory Legal Announcement in a Gazette of Legal Notices (Journal d'Annonces Légales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorised by the prefecture of the department in which the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French legal announcement containing company name, corporate form (SAS), data of the registration, share capital amount, registered-office address, corporate object, and the President's name. Submit the text to the selected JAL; pay the publication fee; obtain the attestation de parution (certificate of publication) to be attached to the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Draft legal announcement text
Copy of the Statuts
Bank certificate of deposit of share capital
Registered-office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL newsletter rejects the announcement for incompleteness or inconsistencies, correct the text and republish at an authorised journal; the re-publication fee applies but no penalty if prior to the Guichet Unique submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Complete Incorporation Dossier through the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique de l'INPI via the online portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet Unique and select SAS (Société par Actions Simplifiée). Enter all corporate legal data; upload the executed Statuts, the bank certificate of funds deposit, the JAL attestation de parution, the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE for each shareholder with a participation exceeding 25%), and the declaration of non-condemnation of the President and General Manager. Pay the due taxes and registry fees electronically; submit and retain the INPI electronic receipt of filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Statuts (PDF)
Certificate of deposit of share capital issued by the bank
Attestation de parution from the JAL
Declaration concerning the beneficial owner (Formulaire RBE)
Declaration on honour / non-condemnation (déclaration sur l'honneur) by the President
Justification and consent of the owner of the registered-office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique challenges the dossier for missing or illegible documents, correct the omissions within 15 days of the notification of incompleteness; re-submission through the playful portal at no additional fee. In case of substantial deficiencies, the dossier is automatically terminated and a new filing is required after drafting a corrective deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the RCS and Issuance of the Kbis Extract / SIREN-SIRET
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce de la localisation du siège social (Commercial Court Registry of the registered office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Greffe verifies the legality and completeness of the dossier received from the Guichet Unique, validates the incorporation, allocates the SIREN/SIRET number and extracts, and issues the extract of the Registration du Commerce et des Sociétés (Kbis) that constitutes the official proof of the company's legal existence. The nationwide registry number is published in the official databases (Infogreffe / Annuaire des Entreprises).
required_dossiers: INPI Guichet Unique acknowledgment and certificate
Statutory incorporation dossier as registered
Power of attorney of the legal-agent filing if signature mandate is given
Registration fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a refusal decision (décision de rejet), corporate counsel may challenge it before the presiding judge of the commercial court in a formal conciliation and referral procedure; alternatively, the correcting amendments (curative instrument) may be refiled through the Guichet Unique within 30 days to restart verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, VAT and Payment-Rails Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) for VAT and corporate tax numbering; commercial payment providers Stripe / PayPal for settlement rails.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Kbis, the statutory tax authority automatically assigns the French VAT identification number (TVA intracommunautaire) and the company is registered for corporate income tax (IS). Submit the Kbis to Stripe and PayPal via the respective underwriting portals, providing the SIRET number, French VAT number, legal-form document, bank details of the operational current account (after releasing blocked funds), and ultimate beneficial ownership information. Complete the DGCCRF distance-selling information obligations in the online store's terms and conditions. If pet food is commercialised, register with the DDPP / DD(CS)PP as a feed-hygiene establishment under Regulation (EC) No 183/2005.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract (issued less than 3 months prior)
SIRET number confirmation
Intra-community VAT number (FR[...]) confirmation letter from DGFiP
Bank unblocking certificate (mainlevée de blocage) and current-account IBAN
Beneficial-owner attestation of shareholders holding more than 25% (KYC for Stripe/PayPal)
Certificate of registration as feed-hygiene establishment (only if the product catalogue includes pet food / animal feed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not allocated automatically, apply electronically for issuance via the DGFiP form (procedures of the national e-service); if Stripe/PayPal rejects the KYC or risk review, rectify the identity documents, provide the French IBAN before 2 weeks, and solicit the payment service provider's compliance department for a balance-assessment; if a pet-food import feed-hygiene registration is refused by the DDPP, correct the HACCP dossier and re-apply within the administrative appeal period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) for consumer protection and unfair-trade monitoring; Direction Départementale de l'Emploi, du Travail, des Solidarités et de la Protection des Populations (DDETSPP) for pet-food hygiene registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating license is required; the sole mandatory operating authorization is the RCS registration evidenced by the Kbis extract (French NAF code 4791B — online mail-order retailing), complemented, if applicable, by the DDPP feed-hygiene establishment registration for pet food.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) of the region in which any logistics warehouse is situated, acting for the Ministry for Ecological Transition.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — dispatch-only electronic retailing of pet supplies does not trigger any mandatory environmental impact assessment; if enclosed storage of non-hazardous products exceeds 1,500 m², the activity enters the ICPE declaration tier (rubrique 1510) under the order of 12 June 2021; ordinary parcels under this threshold require no filing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or combustion VOCs are generated by e-commerce logistics; compliance with the ICPE order applying to covered warehouses is mandatory if threshold 1,500 m² is crossed (storm-water retention and treatment, segregated waste sorting and removal of non-hazardous waste, fire-water retention). Packaging waste obligations apply under the Anti-Waste and Circular Economy Act (AGEC), including registration with CITEO or ECOLOGICO for eco-modulation on packaging sold to final consumers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Under the French Labour Code, the company must maintain a Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) covering both head-office and warehouse employees before operations begin; general fire-safety measures (extinguishers, escape routes, periodic checks) and electrical-installation conformity certificates are required in any leased workplace. If the warehouse or showroom is open to the public, the relevant ERP fire-safety registration applies. There are no structural-load permits specific to e-commerce storage below the ICPE warehouse threshold; building permit requirements only apply if the tenant carries out covered internal refurbishments of more than 150 m², in which case a prior declaration is filed with the municipal urbanism authority.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — French Public Finance Directorate; portal: impots.gouv.fr / Pro à Pro; VAT registrations via formalities entreprises (INSEE / guichet unique)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register for French VAT via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) before commencing taxable activity, unless they are within the EU OSS regime (in which case they register in the member state of establishment). The process requires submission of certificate of incorporation, proof of foreign tax residence (PE or non-established status), and EORI number if importing. The DGFiP issues a French VAT number (Numéro d'Identification TVA, FR + 11 digits). Failure to register triggers penalties and retrospective VAT assessment from the first taxable transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — French SAS is fully taxable in France at the standard corporate income tax (IS) rate (25% from 2022 onward, reduced rates for small businesses on the first EUR 42,500 of profit). As a tax resident entity, it is subject to worldwide income, with territorial exemptions under tax treaties. There is no pass-through election for SAS. The SAS is not eligible for US-style check-the-box; French law imposes fixed taxation under the Code Général des Impôts (CGI) Art. 206.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under French law. The only relevant elections are (i) VAT option for the franchise en base de TVA (small business exemption) for taxpayers whose turnover is below EUR 85,000 for goods (art. 293 B CGI), which is a derogation and generally not recommended for exports for refund purposes; (ii) Tax consolidation from the 5th year under Article 223 A CGI (integrated fiscal regime); (iii) Election for territoriality of profits under Article 209 B for foreign branches (rare). Hybrid mismatch rules apply under ATAD implementation (CGI Art. 212 bis) to deny deductions in cross-border mismatch situations; no elective mitigation is available except alignment of entity treatment in the counterparty jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for French VAT; any taxable person making taxable supplies in France must register, regardless of turnover, unless the EU OSS scheme applies (distance sales threshold EUR 10,000 across all EU member states for an EU-established business; non-EU businesses have no threshold and must register from the first sale unless OSS immaterial). For a French SAS (a French entity), VAT registration is mandatory from the first transaction, subject to franchise en base exemption threshold (EUR 85,000 for goods, EUR 37,500 for services) which is optional and generally not exercised for export-orientated e-commerce activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing a phased mandatory e-invoicing rollout effective 1 September 2026 (deferred from July 2024). All VAT- taxable persons established in France must receive e-invoices through a certified PDP (Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire) or the public portal (Chorus Pro). Clearance is not real-time fiscal stamping; the French model uses continuous transmission and data reporting (e-reporting) within one business day. API requirements are defined by DGFiP specifications; e-invoices must be formatted in Factur-X, UBL, or CII. For outbound sales to non-French businesses, e-reporting of cross-border invoices is mandatory. Failure to comply results in EUR 15 per invoice penalty (capped EUR 15,000 per year) and additional 5% late filing penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAT at 0% applies to exports of goods supplied from France to outside the EU (Article 262-I-1 CGI) and to intra-Community supplies of goods (Article 262-0-bis CGI) provided that the goods are dispatched or transported to another EU member state and the supplier retains proof of transport. For e-commerce retail of physical pet products, the transport must be completed by the seller (or a carrier on his behalf) to a destination outside France but within the EU; for exports outside the EU, the goods must leave the EU customs territory within the statutory period. Pet supplies (pet food and non-veterinary care devices) are standard-rated goods; however, zero-rating is applied strictly on the movement of the goods, not on the nature of the product, except for qualifying animal feedingstuffs which may be eligible for reduced 5.5% rate (art. 278 bis) if classified as feeds – but for export zero-rating, movement criterion governs. Offshore services (e.g., digital services) to non-EU customers are outside the scope of French VAT under Article 259 B CGI (B2B section 196 directive) or subject to the place of supply rule (the customer's location).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (document administratif unique / DAU) or EXA for e-commerce shipments, with validated exit confirmation by customs (MRN status)
Bill of Lading (B/L) or air waybill / transport document evidencing physical dispatch from France to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank transfer / foreign exchange receipt) proving payment from the non-EU customer (for proof of consideration and customs value consistency)
Contract or purchase order from the foreign customer
Proof of transport (carrier invoices, logistics tracking with destination proof, CMR notes for road transport)
For intra-community supplies: a valid French intra-community declaration (EC lists) and a valid customer VAT registration number validated via VIES
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP audits export zero-rating claims with high scrutiny, especially in e-commerce where suspected artificial export schemes ('carrousel') are common. If the exporter cannot substantiate the actual physical removal from the EU or the intra-community nature of the transaction, the VAT becomes due at the standard rate, subject to the 20% surcharge for serious inaccuracies (40% for deliberate fraud, 80% for abusive fraud or obstruction) plus interest at 0.20% per month. Clawback is applied retrospectively for up to 3 years (6 years in case of undisclosed activity, 10 years in certain fraud situations, and no time limit for VAT fraud involving criminal offence). In addition, personal liability may be imposed on the SAS legal representative under article L. 267 LPF for tax debts resulting from grossly negligent or fraudulent management. On conviction for VAT fraud (tax evasion), penalties can reach EUR 75,000 and 2 years imprisonment per individual; corporate fines are at EUR 375,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, operating within the Eurosystem framework under the European Central Bank's monetary authority and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) for investment-screening and balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions. Under EU primary and secondary law, no exchange-control approval is required for cross-border payments, profit remittances, or capital movements. Profit repatriation is unrestricted, subject only to standard corporate income tax withholding rules, anti-abuse treaty checks, and France's domestic tax-residency substance requirements. The euro is fully legal-tender and freely transferable across the Single Euro Payments Area and global SWIFT network.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion requirement exists for export receipts in France. There is no prescribed timeline for repatriation and no obligation to convert foreign currency into euros. Exporters may retain foreign currency accounts domestically or abroad, subject to ordinary tax declaration obligations and transfer-pricing documentation if related parties are involved.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB / Crédit Agricole S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: EU-licensed Electronic Money Institutions and payment institutions are viable as supplementary collection/settlement rails under the PSD2 passporting regime. Non-EEA EMIs, particularly UK-licensed firms post-Brexit, are not automatically passported and maintain only limited viability as ancillary channels, not substitutes for a French/EU-licensed banking relationship. Use of such EMIs must not obscure the underlying beneficial ownership of funds and must be fully disclosed in the corporate account application to French banks to prevent AML-kyc rejection. Overall feasibility rating: Medium for EU-passported EMIs; Low for offshore non-EU EMIs acting as principal treasury settlement accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French anti-money-laundering regulations require robust customer due diligence but do not categorically mandate a physical interview. In practice, leading French banks require the legal representatives and material beneficial owners to attend an in-person identity verification and business-rationale meeting at a French branch, or to complete a remote video-based KYC interview accepted under the bank's approved compliance procedure. Remote opening is permitted only when the bank has certified identity-verification technology and the corporate structure is aligned with the bank's risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or legal representative linked to high-risk or under-resourced non-EEA jurisdictions, or concentrated shareholder power outside the EEA.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate shareholding chain with notarized apostilled certificates, audited financial statements, personal passports of all material beneficial owners, functional CVs for senior management, residential title/lease evidence, tax residency certificates for all UBOs, and a written narrative explaining business rationale for non-resident ownership and the operational substance of the French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared e-commerce activity and current-year transaction projections through multiple payment service providers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial agreements with Stripe and PayPal or their registered EU partners, settlement statements for the past three to six months, projected cash-flow model linking card settlements to inventory purchases and logistics, French VAT registration confirmation (unless below SME threshold), and publicly available e-commerce storefront evidence showing genuine pet product sales.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection expected from non-EEA related parties, particularly when the amount exceeds the SAS minimum capital requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed equity subscription and share-issuance minutes, bank reference letters from the remitting institution, source of wealth statements, tax and legal status of the contributing entity, transfer-pricing documentation for intra-group financing, a formal declaration that the contribution is equity not debt, and confirmation of proper filing of Banque de France balance-of-payments statistics for direct investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concurrent use of multiple EMIs and PSPs creating opaque fund flows and aggregated cross-border activity inconsistent with France's banking expectation of a single dominant treasury ledger.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy memorandum listing all PSPs and EMIs, merchant credentials with each provider, quarterly reconciliation reports between PSP settlement currencies and bank statements, an AML-compliant internal control mapping, and a certification signed by the SAS managing director confirming that all PSP accounts are pledged under the same French accounting system and auditable by the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use standard SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated inbound contributions from EEA countries. For non-EEA remittances, require a SWIFT MT103 with full remitter and beneficiary identity, purpose code matching 'direct investment' or 'equity capital' under the French balance-of-payments classification, and attach the corporate resolution and subscription agreement. For capital injections exceeding approximately EUR 150,000 from non-residents, the SAS must file a direct investment declaration with the Banque de France for statistical purposes; the transaction does not require prior authorisation unless the target sector is regulated. All inbound funds must be clearly credited to the capital escrow sub-account before the notary or registry filing of the SAS's capital increase or incorporation statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade payments to foreign suppliers, use SWIFT MT103 for outside EUR/SEPA zones, SEPA Credit Transfer for intra-EEA suppliers in euros, and irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (via correspondent bank MT700 series) for large inventory orders requiring documentary risk mitigation. High-frequency small-ticket supplier payments in pet products are typically settled by cross-border card or open-account via SWIFT customer credit transfers using purpose code 'imports of goods' (statistical motive 'importation de marchandises'). Payments must be routed solely through the cleared French banking account to maintain audit trail and avoid PSP-splitting red flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain Vanilla EUR/foreign-currency forward contracts (forfait sec) with a licensed French bank or EU-authorised investment firm
Outright FX swaps for rolling trade-settlement exposure
Zero-cost collars (futures options combination) permitted as hedging instruments for underlying commercial receivables/payables
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible jurisdictional currencies, subject to underlying trade exposure demonstration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and deposit of annual financial statements (comptes annuels) with the Register of Commerce; publication of the deposit attachment and, if opted, confidentiality declaration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI) / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of fiscal-year close; RCS deposit within 1 month after approval. For a calendar-year SAS, the ordinary outside deadline is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Greffe formal injunction; court-ordered astreinte up to EUR 1,500 per day; criminal fine up to EUR 3,000 for SAS officers; repeated non-filing exposes the entity to judicial redress and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (déclaration n°2065-SD/2572-SD) with financial statements annex, fixed-assets, depreciation and tax-rates schedules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – Service des Impôts des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal-year close; for a 31 December closing, administrative extension to 3 May of the following year, or the next business day if 3 May is a holiday.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of unpaid corporate income tax, increased to 40% for deliberate conduct or 80% for fraudulent conduct, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; cumulative penalties may block clean annual declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO and corporate-record update in the RCS (déclaration rectificative des bénéficiaires effectifs) when any shareholding or control change occurs during the year; the RCS file must be current at every annual filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (INPI) / RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any event modifying beneficial-ownership data; nil-change companies are not exempt from verifying accuracy at each RCS formality.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative blocking of RCS formalities; fine up to EUR 7,500; persistent inaccurate UBO data exposes directors to individual liability and strike-off procedures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) for a SAS that, in the last closed financial year, exceeds two of the three following thresholds: total balance sheet above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average staff exceeding 50. Voluntary audit remains possible under the articles or at shareholders' request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Local GAAP (ANC Regulation No. 2014-03 as amended, including the Plan Comptable Général); IFRS may be used only for consolidated financial statements of listed groups and is not permitted for the SAS individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No independent annual UBO confirmation statement exists in France; the RCS contains the UBO declaration and any change requires an updated declaration within 30 days. For annual compliance, the company must, at each filing, confirm that the beneficial-owner file is unchanged and consistent with the share register; a documented nil-change review is recommended even if no separate filing is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
